title: Psalms Chapter 122 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 122 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 122 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 122.

questions.question: According to Psalms 122:1, what caused the speaker to be glad?
options: When they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the LORD
When the gates of Jerusalem were opened
When the tribes of Israel gathered
questions.correctAnswer: When they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:1 states the speaker was glad specifically when they said 'Let us go into the house of the LORD.'

questions.question: In Psalms 122:2, where do our feet stand?
questions.correctAnswer: Within the gates of Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:2 clearly says, 'Our feet shall stand within thy gates, O Jerusalem.'

questions.question: How is Jerusalem described in Psalms 122:3?
options: As a city that is compact together
As a city surrounded by water
questions.correctAnswer: As a city that is compact together
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:3 describes Jerusalem as 'a city that is compact together.'

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 122:4, the tribes go up to give thanks unto the name of the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:4 states that the tribes of the LORD go up 'to give thanks unto the name of the LORD.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 122:5, what is set in the house of David?
questions.correctAnswer: Thrones of judgment
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:5 mentions 'thrones of judgment' are set in the house of David.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 122:6 commands us to pray for the peace of Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:6 explicitly says, 'Pray for the peace of Jerusalem.'

questions.question: What will happen to those who love Jerusalem according to Psalms 122:6?
questions.correctAnswer: They shall prosper
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:6 promises prosperity to those who love Jerusalem.

questions.question: According to Psalms 122:7, what is wished within Jerusalem's walls and palaces?
questions.correctAnswer: Peace and prosperity
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:7 says, 'Peace be within thy walls, and prosperity within thy palaces.'

questions.question: True or False: The speaker says in Psalms 122:8 that they will say peace for the sake of their enemies.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:8 says the speaker will say peace for the sake of 'my brethren and companions,' not enemies.

questions.question: In Psalms 122:9, why does the speaker seek the good of Jerusalem?
options: Because of the house of the LORD our God
Because it is a wealthy city
Because it is a city of enemies
Because it is distant and unknown
questions.correctAnswer: Because of the house of the LORD our God
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:9 states the speaker seeks Jerusalem's good because of the house of the LORD our God.

questions.question: Which comes first in Psalms 122: the gladness when being told to go to the house of the LORD or the standing of feet within Jerusalem's gates?
options: Gladness when told to go to the house of the LORD
Standing of feet within Jerusalem's gates
questions.correctAnswer: Gladness when told to go to the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:1 mentions gladness first, followed by standing within gates in Psalms 122:2.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 122 describes Jerusalem as a city that is divided and scattered.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:3 describes Jerusalem as 'a city that is compact together,' not divided or scattered.

questions.question: According to Psalms 122:5, who has thrones of judgment set in the city?
questions.correctAnswer: The house of David
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:5 mentions the thrones of judgment are set in the house of David.

questions.question: What do the tribes of the LORD do according to Psalms 122:4?
options: They go up unto the testimony of Israel to give thanks to the LORD
They build altars in the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: They go up unto the testimony of Israel to give thanks to the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:4 states the tribes go up to give thanks unto the name of the LORD.

questions.question: What is the reason given in Psalms 122:9 for seeking the good of Jerusalem?
options: Because of the house of the LORD our God
questions.correctAnswer: Because of the house of the LORD our God
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:9 explains the good of Jerusalem is sought on account of the house of the LORD our God.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 122 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 122 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 122:4, why do the tribes of the LORD go up to Jerusalem?
options: To give thanks unto the name of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: To give thanks unto the name of the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:4 states that the tribes of the LORD go up to Jerusalem to give thanks unto the name of the LORD. This reflects the practice of worship and gratitude to God in the city of Jerusalem.

questions.question: What does Psalms 122:5 say about the thrones in Jerusalem?
options: They are set thrones of judgment
They are hidden in secret chambers
questions.correctAnswer: They are set thrones of judgment
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:5 describes the thrones as set thrones of judgment, specifically the thrones of the house of David, highlighting Jerusalem's role as a center of divine and royal authority.

questions.question: What instruction does Psalms 122:6 give regarding Jerusalem?
options: Pray for the peace of Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Pray for the peace of Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:6 instructs believers to pray for the peace of Jerusalem, emphasizing the importance of intercession and peace for the city that holds spiritual significance.

questions.question: What promise is given in Psalms 122:6 to those who love Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: They shall prosper
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:6 promises prosperity to those who love Jerusalem, linking love for the city with tangible blessings and success.

questions.question: How does Psalms 122:4-5 connect the tribes of Israel with the house of David?
options: The tribes ignore the house of David
The tribes go to give thanks and the house of David has judgment thrones set
The house of David is separate from the tribes
The tribes rebel against the house of David
questions.correctAnswer: The tribes go to give thanks and the house of David has judgment thrones set
questions.explanation: Verses 4 and 5 show that the tribes ascend to Jerusalem to give thanks to the LORD, where the house of David holds set thrones of judgment, signifying unity in worship and governance.

questions.question: What practical Christian virtue is highlighted by the instruction in Psalms 122:6 to 'Pray for the peace of Jerusalem'?
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer and intercession
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:6 emphasizes the virtue of prayer and intercession, encouraging believers to actively seek peace through prayer for a city of great spiritual importance.

questions.question: According to Psalms 122:7, what two things are wished to be within Jerusalem’s walls and palaces?
questions.correctAnswer: Peace and prosperity
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:7 expresses the desire for peace within Jerusalem’s walls and prosperity within its palaces, reflecting a holistic blessing of safety and abundance.

questions.question: How does Psalms 122:8 demonstrate the importance of community among believers?
options: By saying peace be within thee for brethren and companions' sakes
questions.correctAnswer: By saying peace be within thee for brethren and companions' sakes
questions.explanation: Verse 8 shows that peace is desired not only for oneself but also for brethren and companions, highlighting the value of fellowship and communal harmony.

questions.question: What motivates the psalmist in Psalms 122:9 to seek the good of Jerusalem?
options: Because of the house of the LORD our God
questions.correctAnswer: Because of the house of the LORD our God
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:9 reveals that the psalmist’s motivation to seek Jerusalem’s good stems from reverence for the house of the LORD, linking spiritual devotion with practical concern.

questions.question: What does Psalms 122:4 teach about the relationship between worship and gratitude?
options: Worship includes giving thanks to the name of the LORD
Gratitude is shown only through sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: Worship includes giving thanks to the name of the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 4 links the ascent of the tribes for testimony and worship with the act of giving thanks, teaching that true worship involves expressing gratitude to God.

questions.question: If believers follow the instruction to pray for the peace of Jerusalem in Psalms 122:6, what result does verse 7 promise?
options: Peace and prosperity will be within the city
questions.correctAnswer: Peace and prosperity will be within the city
questions.explanation: Verse 6 instructs prayer for peace, and verse 7 promises that peace and prosperity will be established within Jerusalem’s walls and palaces as a result of such intercession.

questions.question: How does Psalms 122:5 encourage believers to view God's justice?
options: As established and authoritative through the house of David
questions.correctAnswer: As established and authoritative through the house of David
questions.explanation: Verse 5 describes the thrones of judgment set in the house of David, signaling that God’s justice is firmly established and exercised through divinely appointed authority.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 122:2 emphasizes that the psalmist’s feet shall stand outside the gates of Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:2 states that 'Our feet shall stand within thy gates, O Jerusalem,' indicating presence inside the city, not outside.

questions.question: True or False: Based on Psalms 122:9, the psalmist’s concern for Jerusalem is rooted in God's presence there.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 9 explicitly states that the psalmist seeks the good of Jerusalem because of the house of the LORD our God, indicating God’s presence as the motivation.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 122:3, Jerusalem is described as a city that is scattered and divided.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:3 describes Jerusalem as 'builded as a city that is compact together,' meaning it is united and well-joined, not scattered or divided.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 122 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 122.

questions.question: What does the psalmist pray for concerning Jerusalem in Psalms 122:7?
options: Peace within its walls and prosperity within its palaces
questions.correctAnswer: Peace within its walls and prosperity within its palaces
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:7 explicitly states, 'Peace be within thy walls, and prosperity within thy palaces,' showing the psalmist's prayer for both peace and prosperity for Jerusalem.

questions.question: In Psalms 122:8, why does the psalmist say, 'Peace be within thee'?
options: For my brethren and companions' sakes
To celebrate the feast of tabernacles
questions.correctAnswer: For my brethren and companions' sakes
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:8 states the reason clearly: 'For my brethren and companions' sakes, I will now say, Peace be within thee.' This shows the communal concern for peace.

questions.question: According to Psalms 122:9, what motivates the psalmist to seek the good of Jerusalem?
options: Because of the house of the LORD our God
To gain favor with the king
questions.correctAnswer: Because of the house of the LORD our God
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'Because of the house of the LORD our God I will seek thy good,' indicating a spiritual motivation tied to God's dwelling.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of praying for the peace of Jerusalem as found in Psalms 122:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Nehemiah 2:17
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 2:17 records Nehemiah's concern for Jerusalem's welfare and peace, paralleling Psalms 122:6's prayer for the peace of Jerusalem.

questions.question: Which New Testament book contains a similar exhortation to seek the peace of Jerusalem, reflecting Psalms 122:6 and 9?
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:14 speaks of seeking the city which has foundations, referring implicitly to Jerusalem and the spiritual peace sought in Psalms 122:6 and 9.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Psalms 122:7-9 to emphasize the desire for peace and prosperity?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: These verses show synonymous parallelism, repeating similar ideas about peace and prosperity, a common feature in Hebrew poetry.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated 'peace' in Psalms 122:7 and 8 is 'shalom.' What is the fuller meaning of 'shalom' beyond simple peace?
questions.correctAnswer: Completeness, welfare, and harmony
questions.explanation: In Hebrew, 'shalom' means not just peace but also completeness and well-being, reflecting a holistic blessing as in Psalms 122:7-8.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 122 was written by Solomon as a prayer for the newly built temple in Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 122 is attributed to David (Psalms 122:1), not Solomon, and is a song of degrees expressing joy about going to the house of the LORD, rather than a prayer for the temple's construction.

questions.question: True or False: The phrase 'for my brethren and companions' sakes' in Psalms 122:8 suggests a communal or corporate aspect to the psalmist's prayer.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:8 shows the psalmist praying for peace not just for himself but for his community, highlighting the collective concern for Jerusalem's welfare.

questions.question: Which verse in Psalms 122 describes Jerusalem as 'builded as a city that is compact together'?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalms 122:3
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:3 states, 'Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together,' describing its unity and strength.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'thrones of judgment' mentioned in Psalms 122:5?
options: They represent the authority of the house of David
They are the seats of foreign kings
They refer to the priestly courts
questions.correctAnswer: They represent the authority of the house of David
questions.explanation: Psalms 122:5 says, 'For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David,' indicating royal judicial authority in Jerusalem.

questions.question: How does Psalms 122:4 describe the tribes of Israel's movement toward Jerusalem?
options: Going up to the testimony of Israel to give thanks unto the name of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Going up to the testimony of Israel to give thanks unto the name of the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 4 speaks of the tribes ascending to Jerusalem for worship and thanksgiving, a pilgrimage to the LORD's testimony.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'Our feet shall stand within thy gates, O Jerusalem' in Psalms 122:2 symbolize?
options: Arrival and participation in worship at the city
questions.correctAnswer: Arrival and participation in worship at the city
questions.explanation: Standing within the gates signifies entering Jerusalem to join in worship and communal religious life, as per Psalms 122:2.

questions.question: Which literary technique frames Psalms 122, beginning and ending with references to joy and seeking the good of Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The psalm begins with gladness (verse 1) and ends with seeking Jerusalem's good (verse 9), framing the psalm with a literary inclusio.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of Jerusalem as a spiritual city to be sought, complementing Psalms 122's focus on the physical city?
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 12:22-24
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:22-24 contrasts Mount Zion and the heavenly Jerusalem, echoing Psalms 122’s theme of the city of God to be sought.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 122 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 122 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What is the initial emotional response David expresses upon hearing the invitation to go to the house of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Gladness
questions.explanation: David states in Psalms 122:1 that he was glad when they said unto him, 'Let us go into the house of the LORD,' indicating joy in approaching God’s presence.

questions.question: According to Psalms 122:2, where shall the feet of the worshippers stand?
questions.correctAnswer: Within the gates of Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Verse 2 teaches that their feet shall stand within the gates of Jerusalem, signifying entering the sacred city where God’s presence dwells.

questions.question: What is the significance of Jerusalem being 'builded as a city that is compact together' in Psalms 122:3?
options: It symbolizes unity and divine order among God's people
It represents political power and military strength
It indicates isolation from other nations
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes unity and divine order among God's people
questions.explanation: Verse 3 describes Jerusalem as a city compact together, reflecting the theological theme of communal unity and God's orderly reign among His covenant people.

questions.question: Psalms 122:4 references tribes going up to Jerusalem for what purpose?
options: To give thanks unto the name of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: To give thanks unto the name of the LORD
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states the tribes come to give thanks unto the name of the LORD, emphasizing worship and covenantal gratitude.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is emphasized by the mention of 'thrones of judgment' in Psalms 122:5?
options: The doctrine of divine justice and kingly authority
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of divine justice and kingly authority
questions.explanation: Verse 5's 'thrones of judgment' signify God's sovereign rule through David’s house, revealing divine justice and authoritative governance.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated by the prayer for the peace of Jerusalem in Psalms 122:6?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s peace-keeping presence
questions.explanation: Praying for peace in verse 6 highlights God's attribute as the source and sustainer of shalom and well-being among His people.

questions.question: What promise is linked to those who love Jerusalem according to Psalms 122:6?
questions.correctAnswer: They shall prosper
questions.explanation: The verse asserts that those who love Jerusalem will prosper, indicating God’s blessing on those aligned with His covenant community.

questions.question: How does Psalms 122:7 describe the desired state within Jerusalem's walls and palaces?
options: Peace within the walls and prosperity within the palaces
Conflict within the walls and poverty in the palaces
Silence within the walls and decay in the palaces
Chaos within the walls and desolation in the palaces
questions.correctAnswer: Peace within the walls and prosperity within the palaces
questions.explanation: Verse 7 explicitly prays for peace and prosperity within Jerusalem’s physical and social structures, underscoring God’s blessing on the city.

questions.question: What motivated David’s declaration of 'Peace be within thee' in Psalms 122:8?
options: Because of his brethren and companions
questions.correctAnswer: Because of his brethren and companions
questions.explanation: David's motivation expressed in verse 8 is the wellbeing of his brethren and companions, showing the communal concern in covenant life.

questions.question: Which doctrine is taught by David’s desire to seek the good of Jerusalem for 'the house of the LORD our God' in Psalms 122:9?
options: Sanctification and intercession for the covenant community
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification and intercession for the covenant community
questions.explanation: Verse 9 reflects a sanctifying concern and intercessory prayer for Jerusalem’s welfare because of God’s presence, a mark of covenantal holiness and care.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Psalms 122:4 and Psalms 122:5 convey about God's kingdom?
options: God’s kingdom is both worshipful and judicial, centered on Israel and David’s throne
God’s kingdom is purely spiritual with no earthly manifestation
God’s kingdom is limited to the temple rituals alone
questions.correctAnswer: God’s kingdom is both worshipful and judicial, centered on Israel and David’s throne
questions.explanation: Verse 4 highlights worship by the tribes, while verse 5 reveals judicial authority through David’s thrones, together illustrating the dual aspects of God's kingdom.

questions.question: What theological insight arises when synthesizing Psalms 122:6 and Psalms 122:7 about the nature of peace?
options: Peace is comprehensive, encompassing both spiritual well-being and material prosperity
Peace only refers to spiritual calmness
Peace means absence of enemies only
questions.correctAnswer: Peace is comprehensive, encompassing both spiritual well-being and material prosperity
questions.explanation: Verse 6 connects peace with prosperity for those who love Jerusalem, and verse 7 details peace within walls and prosperity within palaces, showing peace’s full societal scope.

questions.question: Combining Psalms 122:1 and Psalms 122:9, what do we learn about the believer’s motivation for worship and intercession?
options: Joy in approaching God and a desire for the welfare of God’s house
Fear of judgment and avoidance of sin
Desire for material gain and social status
questions.correctAnswer: Joy in approaching God and a desire for the welfare of God’s house
questions.explanation: Verse 1 shows gladness at going to the LORD’s house, and verse 9 reveals a heartfelt seeking of Jerusalem’s good because of God’s house, linking worship with intercession.

questions.question: How does Psalms 122:3’s description of Jerusalem relate to the biblical narrative of redemption?
options: It foreshadows the unified community of redeemed people in the New Jerusalem
It describes a temporary political alliance
It refers only to Solomon’s city planning
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the unified community of redeemed people in the New Jerusalem
questions.explanation: The compactness of Jerusalem symbolizes unity which points ahead to the eschatological New Jerusalem in Revelation, representing redeemed humanity’s perfect fellowship.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that prayers for the peace of Jerusalem are merely nationalistic and have no spiritual relevance. What does Psalms 122:6-9 actually teach about this prayer?
options: The prayer reflects a spiritual concern rooted in God's covenant presence and communal holiness
The prayer is purely political and secular
The prayer is a call for military conquest
The prayer is a poetic metaphor without real intent
questions.correctAnswer: The prayer reflects a spiritual concern rooted in God's covenant presence and communal holiness
questions.explanation: Verses 6-9 show that praying for Jerusalem’s peace is motivated by love for God’s house and community, not nationalism, affirming a spiritual and covenantal dimension (cf. Romans 15:32, Ephesians 6:18).
